title: Deploying a DAG
summary: How an edited graph becomes a running execution. The middle row is authoring and approval in Laravel, the row below is the runtime applying it and answering. The top row is what stops a draft before activation; the bottom row is what the runtime refuses, at activation or later.

boxes.label: Edit the draft
boxes.detail: A binding gives a role name to one parameter of one device and records the device's applied configuration, its applied generation, the data type, the unit and how long a reading stays fresh. Nodes refer to bindings by role.

boxes.label: Save draft
boxes.detail: Laravel checks that each bound parameter belongs to the named configuration and that a commanded setting has an approved command mapping and a valid value, then asks the runtime to compile. A valid graph is stored with its hash and a revision snapshot. A save against an older draft_revision gets 409, and saving needs automations turned on in the organization. An automation that came with a device move starts here too: a draft at revision 1 with a new UUID, its bindings rewritten onto the new devices, never deployed.

boxes.label: Runtime compile
boxes.detail: 2 to 100 nodes, up to 200 edges and 32 bindings. Ports are typed, each input has exactly one producer, the graph is acyclic, units must agree, branches from different sources meet only in a join, every node must reach an action, and there is at least one action and at most one alert. The result is a canonical definition and its hash.

boxes.label: Diagnostics
boxes.detail: An invalid graph is not saved. Each diagnostic names the node and field at fault, so the editor can mark it.

boxes.label: Activation review
boxes.detail: Before activating, the portal reads each bound device again. For every setting a command node would send, the reviewer approves a grant: the node, the binding, the exact value, a cooldown, a maximum per minute and an optional expiry. A graph with no command node needs no grants.

boxes.label: Stale bindings
boxes.detail: A binding is stale when its configuration, generation, data type or unit is no longer the device's current one, or the device or parameter is gone. The portal blocks activation and offers to move the bindings to the current configuration; the edited draft is then saved and reviewed again.

boxes.label: Deployment snapshot
boxes.detail: The request names an operation UUID, the draft revision and the expected generation; a mismatch or a pending deployment gets 409. Activation is refused while the automation is archived, while it binds a device that moved to another organization, or while automations are off or stopped in the organization. Laravel compiles the draft again with the operation UUID as its version, checks every bound device is active on the bound configuration and generation, and checks the grants and the approver's Device.command. The deployment row is immutable: definition, hash and grants.

boxes.label: Deploy message
boxes.detail: Written to the outbox in the same transaction: operation, workflow and organization UUIDs, generation, target (active or inactive) and the definition, which is empty for inactive. A deactivation caused by a device move records why on its deployment row (moved or device_moved). The workflow becomes pending, and actions of earlier deployments that are still waiting are cancelled.

boxes.label: Runtime activation
boxes.detail: Under a lock on the workflow's head row: a generation at or below the stored one changes nothing, and a snapshot whose identity does not match the request is rejected. The runtime compiles the definition itself and checks every binding against the device it stores. On success it stops the earlier execution (superseded, or disabled for an inactive target) and inserts the new one with its initial state.

boxes.label: Applied
boxes.detail: Laravel matches the outcome to the pending deployment by generation and target, marks it succeeded, records the earlier deployment as superseded and points the workflow's applied deployment at this one. An inactive target stops the earlier deployment as disabled, or with the move's reason, and ends as inactive; when a bound device moved away (device_moved) the workflow shows as suspended instead.

boxes.label: Activation refused
boxes.detail: The diagnostic names the binding's role: binding_changed (the configuration or applied generation is no longer the applied one), device_review_required (the device's source needs review), or unmapped or incompatible binding. Nothing is started and the earlier execution in the runtime is left as it was. Laravel marks the workflow failed, clears the pending operation and shows the diagnostic.

boxes.label: Suspended
boxes.detail: The same binding check runs on every evaluation. When it fails, the runtime disables the execution and reports why; Laravel records binding_changed or device_review_required and shows the workflow as suspended. It does not resume by itself: someone activates it again. A workflow also shows as suspended when a device it binds moved to another organization; Laravel turns it off with a deactivation, and it cannot be activated until that device is removed from its bindings.

steps.text: The author binds device parameters to roles, connects nodes and saves.
Laravel checks the bindings against the device configurations, then the runtime compiles the graph.
An invalid graph comes back as diagnostics that name the node and field. Nothing is saved.
A valid graph is saved as the next draft revision with its definition hash. Activating opens the review.
If a bound device was reconfigured since, its bindings are stale. The portal blocks activation until they are moved to the current configuration.
The reviewer approves one grant per command setting. Laravel compiles once more and freezes the result as a deployment.
The deployment and its workflow.deploy.v2 message commit together. The workflow is now pending.
The runtime claims the message and applies it in one transaction, fenced by the workflow's generation.
If a binding no longer matches the device the runtime stores, or that device needs review, the activation fails with a diagnostic and nothing starts.
Otherwise the earlier execution stops, the new one starts, and workflow.deployment.v1 tells Laravel, which marks the workflow applied.
Bindings are checked again on every evaluation. A later failure suspends the execution until someone activates it again.

An automation carried by a device move enters here in the target organization, as an undeployed draft with a new identity. The move activates it afterwards only if it was running, sends no device commands, its devices are active there, automations are on there and the mover may activate them.
